samples.question: This page shows two solid dark jaws facing each other across a white channel, together with a few small coloured marks. Only the dark ink decides the answer; coloured marks are decoration and never count, even when a coloured mark lies inside the channel. Each jaw is one connected dark piece: an upright bar with a row of straight fingers reaching out across the channel toward the other jaw. The fingers come in facing pairs, one left finger exactly opposite one right finger at the same height, and both jaws have the same top edge and the same bottom edge. Now imagine sliding the right jaw straight to the left, without turning it and without moving it up or down, until the two jaws first touch. The pairs that touch are exactly the pairs whose two fingertips are drawn with the smallest white gap between them; every other pair keeps a gap, and the gap it keeps is the amount by which its drawn gap exceeds that smallest drawn gap. A pair that touches becomes a wall right across the channel; a pair that keeps a gap leaves a passage that white can flow through. Count the closed chambers of white inside the channel: a closed chamber is a piece of the channel with a wall directly above it and a wall directly below it, so white cannot escape from it. The part of the channel above the highest wall opens out at the top of the jaws and the part below the lowest wall opens out at the bottom, so neither of those is a closed chamber. Neither jaw alone fixes any gap: a pair's drawn gap is set by how far its left finger reaches together with how far its right finger reaches. How many fingers the jaws carry, how far any one finger reaches, how far apart the two jaws are drawn, which jaw carries the longer fingers, how thick the fingers are, how much dark ink is on the page, where the jaws sit on the page, and how many coloured marks are drawn never decide the answer. There is always at least one closed chamber and never more than three. How many closed chambers form when the two jaws are pressed together? Answer 1, 2 or 3.
